title: CLAIM: A suppressed Epstein 'client list' exists
summary: Viral '166-name'/'200-name' lists conflate flight logs, the address book and deposition mentions. The July 2025 DOJ/FBI systematic review 'revealed no incriminating client list'; Maxwell told DOJ none exists. No document functioning as a client list has ever been an exhibit in any Epstein/Maxwell case. Existence: UNPROVEN.
tldr: The July 2025 DOJ/FBI memo stated its systematic review found no incriminating 'client list,' no credible evidence of blackmail, and no evidence to investigate uncharged third parties — but the memo is two pages with no published inventory or method, and later releases have substantially expanded the public record.
ai_summary:
AI review of the EpsteinWiki article "The July 2025 DOJ and FBI Epstein Memo: What It Said and What the Records Show" (updated Sept 28, 2026), read in full:
- What the memo says: the two-page July 2025 memo announced reviewers found no incriminating "client list," no credible evidence Epstein blackmailed prominent individuals, no evidence predicating investigation of uncharged third parties, and reaffirmed Epstein died by suicide on August 10, 2019 (SHU video showing nobody entered his tier ~10:40 pm Aug 9 to ~6:30 am Aug 10). It cited 300+ GB of data and physical evidence reviewed and 1,000+ victims, and determined no further disclosure was warranted.
- Critical caveat: "The memo is a statement of agency findings. It is not the underlying investigative file" — it provides no inventory, search protocol, witness analysis, or definition of "client list"; neither page bears a signature or calendar date.
- Important distinctions: "no incriminating client list" does not mean no contact books, calendars, flight records, or witness accounts — "A name in an address book is evidence that contact information was recorded. It is not, by itself, evidence of abuse."
- Earlier context the article flags: December 2019 memo EFTA02731082 shows Southern District of New York prosecutors DID investigate potential co-conspirators and employees after Epstein's indictment — so the July memo's broad third-party statement sits uneasily alongside earlier assessments.
- The no-disclosure stance was overtaken: Congress passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act (November 2025); by January 2026 DOJ said it had published nearly 3.5 million pages plus 2,000+ videos and 180,000 images.
- Summary check: the memo's core claims verified as stated by the article. NOT in this source: the summary's "Maxwell told DOJ none exists" and the "166-name/200-name" list specifics — neither appears in the article.
